items.title: Class Action Lawsuit Filed Against Uber Regarding October 2026 Data Breach
items.summary: A proposed class action lawsuit alleges that Uber Technologies and Fireworks.AI failed to adequately protect sensitive driver information during an October 2026 data breach.
items.content: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Uber Technologies, Inc. and artificial intelligence provider Fireworks.AI, alleging negligence in safeguarding sensitive driver data. The complaint claims that an unauthorized third party accessed Uber's systems through compromised Fireworks.AI credentials, exposing information such as driver's license images, names, addresses, and dates of birth. The lawsuit, filed in November 2026, further alleges that Uber failed to provide timely notification to impacted individuals, waiting approximately one month after the breach was discovered on October 9. Plaintiffs argue that this delay and the company's cybersecurity measures have increased the risk of identity theft and fraud for affected drivers.

items.title: Juries Award Millions in Separate Johnson & Johnson Talc-Related Mesothelioma Lawsuits
items.summary: Two separate juries in Massachusetts and California awarded millions of dollars in damages in lawsuits alleging that Johnson & Johnson's talc-based baby powder caused mesothelioma.
items.content: On November 24, 2026, juries in Massachusetts and California returned verdicts against Johnson & Johnson in separate mesothelioma cases involving the company's talc-based baby powder. A Suffolk County Superior Court jury in Massachusetts awarded approximately $3.3 million, including court-ordered interest, to the family of a plaintiff who developed mesothelioma after years of product use. Separately, a Northern California jury awarded $34.21 million to a plaintiff who also developed mesothelioma after decades of using the company's talc products. In both instances, jurors determined that the company failed to provide adequate warnings regarding the risk of asbestos contamination in its products, which they found to be a substantial factor in the plaintiffs' diagnoses.

items.title: Is Netflix Stock Worth More Than Its Competitors?
items.summary: Netflix (NFLX) keeps more of each sales dollar than almost every company in its peer group. Yet its stock is one of the cheapest in that group. Among five companies, Netflix ranks second on operating margin. It has the fourth-highest price to earnings ratio, which makes it the second cheapest. So is Netflix stock worth more than its competitors.
